title: Pixel Dungeon
lede: Oleg Dolya’s open-source roguelike draws its dungeon, its hero, and its whole interface, from health bar to message log, in coarse enlarged pixels.
summary: A dark stone dungeon with small sprites, a bitmap message log in green and white, and square pixel buttons. Watabou (Oleg Dolya), 2012, GPL 3.

evidence.note: Inspected the developer’s screenshot `level_up.png` as copied to Wikimedia Commons, [Screenshot of Pixel Dungeon.png](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Screenshot_of_Pixel_Dungeon.png), 540 × 888 px. Android version, floor 7.

styles.note: Partial fit: sprites, tiles, bitmap type, and stepped interface frames are all pixel art, but a smooth dark vignette of light and shadow covers the map.

context: Wikipedia calls Pixel Dungeon a 2012 roguelike indie game by Oleg Dolya, first for Android, and says that it is open source and that many games build on its code, most notably Shattered Pixel Dungeon. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_Dungeon).

The GitHub repository, created in July 2014, describes a “Traditional roguelike game with pixel-art graphics and simple interface” and carries the GPL 3.0 license. [GitHub](https://github.com/watabou/pixel-dungeon).
observed: A top-down dungeon of gray stone tiles and dark water on black, with wooden doors and a staircase sign on the walls.
The hero is a small sprite with red hair and a gray tunic. A skeleton, a green bag, and a scroll lie near him.
Text is set in a bitmap face: “+5EXP level up!” in green over the map and a message log in white and green at the bottom.
The top bar has the hero portrait in a square frame, a red health bar with a stepped end, and white pixel counters at the right.
Square gray buttons at the bottom hold pixel icons: a clock, a magnifier, a question mark, a backpack, and a quick slot reading “1/2”.
A smooth, unstepped shadow darkens the map away from the hero and at the edges, and a soft glow surrounds a wall lamp.
interpretation: The game applies one pixel scale to the world and the interface, so the buttons, bars, and text belong to the same grid as the sprites.
The smooth lighting is a later technique laid over the pixel art. It is a branch from the strict 8-bit core, so the fit is partial.
borrow: Draw interface buttons as square tiles with one pixel icon each, on the same pixel scale as the content.
Use two text colors in a log, one for events and one for system messages.

images.alt: Portrait game screenshot: a dark stone dungeon with a red-haired hero sprite, a skeleton, and green text reading plus 5 EXP, level up. A health bar and portrait sit at the top, a green and white message log and square icon buttons at the bottom.
images.caption: Watabou, Pixel Dungeon on Android, level-up screen. Developer screenshot via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Screenshot_of_Pixel_Dungeon.png), GPL 3.

rights.statement: Commons lists the file as GPLv3, author Watabou, 2013, from `https://pixeldungeon.watabou.ru/screens/level_up.png`. The game repository is licensed GPL 3.0.
